body:
## Summary
- Adds optional positional ID arguments to `padz list` so users can filter which pads are displayed: `padz list 2`, `padz list 3 5`, `padz list 1-3`
- Selected pads are shown with their full subtree of children, making it easy to focus on a single pad and its nested items
- Uses the existing `parse_selectors` infrastructure (paths, ranges, title search) for ID resolution

## Details

The primary use case is inspecting nested pads:

```
padz list 3
```
Shows only pad 3 and its children, instead of the full list.

ID filtering composes with existing filters (`--planned`, `--tag`, `--search`, `--deleted`), applied after ID selection.

### Files changed
- **setup.rs**: Added `ids: Vec<String>` positional arg to `List` command
- **handlers.rs**: Threads IDs through handler → ScopedApi → API
- **api.rs**: Parses ID strings into `PadSelector`s via existing `parse_selectors`
- **get.rs**: Core `filter_by_selectors` logic that linearizes the tree, resolves selectors, and extracts matched pads with full subtrees
- **Other command test files**: Updated `get::run` call sites for new signature

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a ready-to-run scaffold that accepts windsurf session CSV uploads, computes analytics, and exposes a common REST API for both web and desktop clients.
- Deliver matching visualizations and PDF reporting so the same dataset can be inspected from a React web UI and a PyQt5 desktop UI.

### Description
- Added a Django + DRF backend with endpoints `POST /api/auth/token/`, `POST /api/upload/`, `GET /api/summary/`, `GET /api/history/`, and `GET /api/report/pdf/` implemented in `backend/analytics/views.py` and routed in `backend/windsurf/urls.py`.
- Implemented CSV validation and analytics in `backend/analytics/services.py` with `validate_columns`, `compute_summary`, `build_chart_buffers`, and `build_pdf_report`, and persisted upload metadata to an `UploadRecord` model that stores the last 5 uploads in SQLite.
- Added a React web client (`web/src/App.js`, `web/package.json`) that performs token login, CSV upload, history fetch, summary display, and Chart.js visualizations (line/bar/pie), and a PyQt5 desktop client (`desktop/app.py`, `desktop/requirements.txt`) with equivalent functionality using Matplotlib.
- Included supporting files: `backend/requirements.txt`, `backend/manage.py`, initial migration, `sample_windsurf_data.csv`, top-level `README.md`, and `.gitignore` for quick local setup.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall backend desktop` to validate Python files compiled successfully, which completed without errors.
- Attempted `cd backend && python manage.py test` but it failed in the current environment due to missing dependencies with the error `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'django'` (install dependencies from `backend/requirements.txt` before running tests).

- Reduce duplicate/stale keyboard listeners and provide a single, stable shortcut handling surface for the game room to avoid re-binding and closure issues.  
- Surface platform-correct keycap UI for sidebar/player list menu items so displayed shortcuts match Mac/Windows labels.  
- Provide an updated third-party library evaluation that includes Socket.dev fetch attempts and a ranked recommendation list.

### Description
- Add a new hook `useGameRoomKeyboardShortcuts` that centralizes keyboard handling and guards editable elements, and add `useGameRoomShortcutDisplayParts` to produce platform-correct keycap strings (`apps/web/src/hooks/useGameRoomKeybindings.ts`).
- Replace the inline `Cmd/Ctrl+K` listener in `CardSearchCommand` with the centralized shortcut system so the command dialog toggles via the shared `searchCards` handler (`apps/web/src/components/CardSearchCommand.tsx`).
- Introduce `GameRoomMainLayout` to wrap sidebar and main area and wire shortcut handlers (`searchCards`, `toggleCommandersPanel`, `openCommanderDamage`) via `useGameRoomKeyboardShortcuts`, and add a `toggleSearchDialog` helper (`apps/web/src/components/GameRoom.tsx`).
- Thread `shortcutParts` into `GameRoomSidebar` and `PlayerList` and render keycap UI for commander-related menu items so the UI shows `⌘` vs `Ctrl` and shift markers appropriately (`apps/web/src/components/GameRoomSidebar.tsx`, `apps/web/src/components/PlayerList.tsx`).
- Add `docs/game-room-keybinding-library-evaluation.md` with ranked recommendations (sorted most → least recommended) and a `Socket.dev` data collection status section noting network limitations observed in this environment.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` which completed successfully.  
- Attempted to fetch Socket.dev package pages with `curl` and programmatic requests and observed `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` for `react-hotkeys-hook`, `tinykeys`, and `hotkeys-js`, so exact Socket.dev score/risk fields could not be retrieved here.  
- Verified the code changes compile-time surface manually by checking modified files and hook signatures (no full CI/lint/typecheck was possible due to external registry/network restrictions).

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

16 H100 GPUs across 2 nodes shared by 15+ team members with manual spreadsheet coordination. Need automated scheduling and resource management.

## Implementation

### Core Components

**Resource Manager** (`gpu_resource_manager.py`)
- Tracks GPU allocation state across cluster nodes
- Allocates/deallocates GPUs to jobs
- Mock implementation for development; ready for Ray integration

**Job Queue** (`job_queue_manager.py`)
- Priority queue with 4 levels (critical/high/normal/low)
- Binary search insertion maintaining sorted order
- State machine: `queued → scheduled → allocating → running → completed/failed`
- Auto-retry on failure (configurable)

**Orchestration Agent** (`orchestration_agent.py`)
- Background async loop polling queue every 5s (configurable)
- Matches available GPUs to pending jobs by priority
- Handles allocation failures and job completion callbacks

### API Surface

```python
# Submit job
POST /queue/submit
{
  "run_id": "exp-1",
  "gpu_count": 4,
  "priority": 3,
  "command": "python train.py"
}

# Start orchestrator
POST /orchestrator/start

# Get status
GET /gpu/status
GET /orchestrator/status
```

11 endpoints total for job lifecycle, priority updates, and orchestrator control.

### Configuration

```bash
export RESEARCH_AGENT_GPU_ORCHESTRATION_ENABLED=true
python server/server.py --workdir /path/to/project
```

Server initializes with 2 nodes × 8 GPUs by default. Orchestrator starts on-demand via API.

### Testing

Unit and integration tests cover:
- Resource allocation/deallocation
- Priority queue ordering
- End-to-end scheduling simulation

Demo scripts included for API usage and workflow.

## Next Steps

- Ray cluster integration for actual job execution
- Frontend UI for monitoring
- Real GPU metrics via nvidia-smi/DCGM

## Summary Security improvements for sandboxed agent API access: 1. **Config redaction** - CLI `config get` now redacts resolved secrets using `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__` sentinel, preventing agents from reading API keys through config resolution 2. **Notion gateway tool** - New tool demonstrating the secure pattern: - Agent calls tool with parameters (action, query, etc.) - Gateway injects API key server-side from `process.env` - Agent never sees the actual secret 3. **Default sandbox allow list** - Added gateway tools that handle secrets server-side: `web_search`, `web_fetch`, `tts`, `notion` ## Problem Sandboxed agents could extract API secrets by: - Calling `config get` to read resolved `${VAR_NAME}` values - The config snapshot returned actual API keys after substitution ## Solution This pattern allows sandboxed agents to use API-dependent tools without exposing credentials. The gateway acts as a secure proxy, injecting secrets server-side while the agent only sees tool results. ### Files Changed - `src/cli/config-cli.ts` - Added redaction before outputting config - `src/agents/tools/notion-tool.ts` - New gateway tool template - `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` - Registered notion tool - `src/agents/sandbox/constants.ts` - Added gateway tools to default allow list ## Test plan - [ ] Verify `openclaw config get` redacts sensitive values - [ ] Test notion tool from sandboxed session - [ ] Confirm agent cannot read `NOTION_API_KEY` directly - [ ] Verify other gateway tools (web_search, tts) work in sandbox 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR tightens secret-handling for sandboxed agents by redacting sensitive config values in `openclaw config get`, adding a Notion “gateway” tool that injects its API key server-side, registering that tool, and expanding the default sandbox allowlist to include gateway-style API tools. The overall direction aligns with existing gateway-side redaction (`redact-snapshot.ts`) and tool registration patterns in `createOpenClawTools`, with the main new surface area being the Notion tool implementation and the updated sandbox tool policy defaults.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Mostly safe to merge, with one functional mismatch in the new Notion tool that will cause createPage failures for database parents. - Core changes (config redaction and allowlist updates) are small and leverage existing redaction utilities. The main risk is the newly introduced Notion gateway tool behavior mismatch where `createPage` cannot actually create under databases despite documentation implying it can. - src/agents/tools/notion-tool.ts

author: danielcherubini
body:
## Summary
Upgrades Diesel ORM from 2.2.4 to 2.3.6 and implements production-ready connection pooling using r2d2. This addresses critical issues with connection management and follows Diesel's best practices.

## Key Changes

### 🔧 Core Infrastructure
- **Upgraded Diesel**: 2.2.4 → 2.3.6 (no breaking changes between versions)
- **Connection Pooling**: Implemented r2d2 with 15 max connections, 30s timeout
- **Shared State**: Added `DbPool` to Serenity's TypeMap for application-wide access
- **Helper Function**: Created `get_pool()` for convenient pool access from context

### 🐛 Critical Fixes
**Background Tasks** - Previously held single database connection forever (major anti-pattern):
- `run_gulag_check()` - Now gets fresh connection each loop iteration with error handling
- `run_gulag_vote_check()` - Same improvement
- Prevents stale connections, timeouts, and bad connection states

### 📦 Database Layer
- Updated all database functions to use `&DbPool` instead of `&mut PgConnection`
- Functions get connections from pool internally
- Removed all `establish_connection()` calls throughout codebase
- Updated message_vote module for pool compatibility

### 🔄 Handler Updates
Updated 15+ handler files to use pool:
- All feature flag checks now pass pool parameter
- AI Slop handler
- All gulag handlers (handler, list, remove, vote, reaction, message command)
- Social media rewriters (Twitter, TikTok, Instagram, Bsky)
- Feature toggles (feat, horny, phony, derpies, elon, teh)
- Server management

## Benefits

### Performance & Reliability
- ✅ **Connection reuse** instead of creating new connections per operation
- ✅ **Automatic lifecycle management** - pool handles reconnections, cleanup
- ✅ **Thread-safe** connection sharing across concurrent Discord events
- ✅ **Production-ready** architecture following industry best practices

### Fixes
- ❌ **Before**: Background tasks held stale connections indefinitely
- ✅ **After**: Fresh connections acquired from pool as needed
- ❌ **Before**: New connection created for every database operation
- ✅ **After**: Connections efficiently reused from pool

## Testing
- ✅ All 38 tests passing
- ✅ Build successful (`cargo build`)
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality
- ✅ Backward compatible - all features work as before

## Configuration
Pool settings in `src/db/mod.rs`:
```rust
Pool::builder()
    .max_size(15)
    .connection_timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))
    .build(manager)
```

These settings are appropriate for a small Discord bot with occasional database operations.

## Migration Notes
- No schema changes required
- No migration files needed
- Drop-in replacement with better performance
- Ready to deploy after merge

## Related Issues
Implements best practices as documented in:
- [Diesel r2d2 Documentation](https://docs.rs/diesel/latest/diesel/r2d2/index.html)
- [Rust PostgreSQL with Diesel Best Practices (2026)](https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-01-26-rust-postgresql-diesel-orm/view)

author: eyycheev
body:
AFFiNE validates the Socket.IO "space:join" payload field "clientVersion". When a non-version string is sent (previously hard-coded to "mcp"), the server may never ACK the join. That hangs WebSocket-based tools: create_doc, append_paragraph, delete_doc.

This change:
- Fetches serverConfig.version via GraphQL (cached) and passes it to joinWorkspace
- Allows manual override via AFFINE_CLIENT_VERSION
- Adds a join timeout and treats ack.data.success === false as failure

Repro: self-hosted AFFiNE serverConfig.version = 0.26.2 (join succeeds with 0.26.2, times out with mcp).

Completes the 7-phase integration plan for Hydrogenesis into Phoenix Archive. Operators now have production-ready implementations with validation, error handling, and comprehensive test coverage.

## Core Changes

### Operator Implementations
- **Enhanced validation**: All operators now validate inputs and raise `ValueError` with clear messages
- **Rich metadata**: Returns include `status`, `pattern`, and contextual metadata instead of raw primitives
- **Type safety**: Added `OperatorStatus` enum and full type hints
- **Error handling**: Graceful handling of edge cases (empty inputs, negative values, missing keys)

Before:
```python
# Hydrogenesi LineageLogic
def apply(self, root: str, generations: int) -> List[str]:
    return [f"{root}::gen-{i}" for i in range(generations)]
```

After:
```python
def apply(self, root: str, generations: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if not root:
        raise ValueError("Root identifier cannot be empty")
    if generations < 0:
        raise ValueError("Generations must be non-negative")
    
    lineage_chain = [f"{root}::gen-{i}" for i in range(generations)]
    return {
        "root": root,
        "generations": generations,
        "lineage_chain": lineage_chain,
        "depth": len(lineage_chain),
        "status": OperatorStatus.COMPLETED.value,
        "pattern": "root_recursion",

```

## Summary

Replace coverage-driven tests with test of behavoir and correctness.

- Replace low-value tests (shape-only assertions, private method tests) with tests that validate real-world behavior
- Consolidate shared fixtures in `conftest.py`, remove 5 dead fixtures, add 4 reusable fixtures (`gen_int_rv`, `hierarchical_normal_noise`, `hierarchical_normal_noise_tight`, `hierarchical_infections`)
- Extract shared non-fixture test code (`ConcreteMeasurements`, `create_mock_infections`) to new `test/test_helpers.py` module
- Test base class no-ops and validation stubs in file `test/test_interface_coverage.py`


## Changes by file

### `test/conftest.py`

Removed 5 dead fixtures, added 4 shared fixtures.

**Dead fixtures removed** (never used by any test file):

- `medium_delay_pmf`
- `counts_process_medium_delay`
- `counts_process_realistic`
- `simple_shedding_pmf`
- `medium_shedding_pmf`

**Dead fixtures removed** (replaced by new shared fixtures):

- `sensor_mode_rv`, `sensor_sd_rv`
- `sensor_mode_rv_tight`, `sensor_sd_rv_tight`

**New shared fixtures added:**

- `gen_int_rv` -- COVID-like 7-day generation interval
- `hierarchical_normal_noise` -- standard HierarchicalNormalNoise with VectorizedRV
- `hierarchical_normal_noise_tight` -- tight variance version for near-deterministic testing
- `hierarchical_infections` -- pre-configured HierarchicalInfections instance

### `test/test_helpers.py` (new file)

Shared non-fixture test code extracted here (since `test/` is a package, `conftest.py` cannot be directly imported by test modules):

- `ConcreteMeasurements` class (concrete implementation of abstract `Measurements` for testing)
- `create_mock_infections()` function (generates spike, constant, or decay infection curves)

### `test/test_temporal_processes.py`

**Added:**

- `test_ar1_mean_reversion` -- verifies AR1 trajectories revert toward zero
- `test_differenced_ar1_trend_persistence` -- verifies DifferencedAR1 produces persistent trends

### `test/test_hierarchical_priors.py`

**Strengthened:**

- Shape-only tests now include value assertions (centering near zero for Normal/StudentT, positivity for Gamma)


### `test/test_hierarchical_infections.py`

**Added:**

- `test_infections_are_positive` -- verifies all infection values are positive (epidemiological invariant)

### `test/test_observation_measurements.py`

**Added:**

- `test_log_scale_correctness` -- verifies output equals log(convolved infections) with known inputs
- `test_sensor_bias_differences` -- verifies hierarchical noise produces sensor-specific biases

**Strengthened:**

- `test_sample_shape` now also verifies sensor variation and log-scale output

### `test/test_observation_counts.py`

**Added:**

- `test_convolution_hand_computable` -- 1000 infections on day 10 with PMF [0.5, 0.5] should produce 500 on days 10 and 11
- `test_observation_passthrough` -- providing `obs=known_values` returns those exact values
- `test_poisson_mean_approximation` -- mean of 50 Poisson samples approximates expected rate

**Strengthened:**

- `test_zero_infections` now asserts `predicted == 0` (not just shape)
- `test_small_infections` now asserts plausible range on predicted values
- `test_sample_returns_correct_shape` now includes non-negative value assertions

### `test/test_pyrenew_builder.py`


**Added:**

- `test_prior_predictive_multi_signal` -- uses `numpyro.infer.Predictive` to draw prior predictive samples from a builder-constructed model; verifies shapes and positivity

**Strengthened:**

Tests interface contracts (__repr__, validate(), infection_resolution(), get_required_lookback()) across implementing classes via parametrized tests

author: nchapman
body:
## Summary

Extracts Playwright's aria snapshot code into a shared `ariaTree` module used by both the CLI (via bundled IIFE) and the browser extension (via direct import). On top of this, adds **Set-of-Marks (SoM)** support for vision mode — when `--vision` is enabled, screenshots now show colored labeled badges on interactive elements so the LLM can visually correlate ref IDs with what it sees.

### What changed

- **Shared ariaTree module** (`src/browser/ariaTree/`): Extracted from Playwright internals into a standalone module with its own types, utilities, and build script. Both CLI and extension consume the same code.
- **Set-of-Marks overlay**: Colored badges (E1, E2, ...) and outlines on interactive elements in screenshots. Structural containers are excluded to reduce noise. Ref assignment moved from tree generation to rendering phase so only visible/interactable elements get refs.
- **Smart interactive element filtering**: SoM badges correctly handle contenteditable, tabindex, multi-value ARIA roles, grid cells/headers, and computed roles via `data-spark-role`.
- **Namespaced DOM attributes**: `aria-ref` → `data-spark-ref` to avoid collisions with page content and ARIA specs.
- **CSP bypass disabled by default**: Playwright's CDP-level injection doesn't need it. `--bypass-csp` flag remains for opt-in.
- **Scroll to element before interaction**: Auto-scrolls targets into view so developers can follow along in headed mode.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run check` — 690 tests passing, formatting and typecheck clean
- [x] Manual test: Chrome + Firefox with `--vision --debug` on apple.com
- [x] Manual test: Amazon multi-step flow (search → sort → extract review)
- [x] Code review + security review — all findings addressed
- [x] Browser expert review of interactive element filtering

body:
## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive E2E tests for Google authentication sign-in flows and improves the reliability of the Google sign-in implementation by prioritizing popup-based authentication over redirect-based flows.

**Key changes:**
- Added 116-line E2E test suite (`google-auth-signin.cy.ts`) covering Google sign-in button rendering across all auth entry points (/auth, /signin, /signup) and full navigation flows
- Refactored `useAuthStore` to prefer `signInWithPopup` over `signInWithRedirect` for better cross-browser compatibility (especially in Safari, Brave, and Firefox with ETP enabled)
- Improved error handling to clear stale `googleRedirectPending` flags and properly handle popup-blocked scenarios
- Updated Cypress base URL from port 5173 to 3000 to match the actual dev server
- Added test IDs to `GoogleSignInButton` component for E2E test selectors
- Updated `.gitignore` to exclude Cypress screenshots and videos

**Why these changes:**
- `signInWithRedirect` silently fails when third-party cookies are blocked, providing poor UX
- Popup-based flow is more reliable across modern browsers and provides immediate user feedback
- Comprehensive E2E tests ensure the sign-in UI remains functional across all auth entry points
- Proper cleanup of session storage prevents false "sign-in failed" toasts on subsequent page loads

## Test Plan

1. Run the new E2E test suite: `pnpm exec cypress run --spec "client/cypress/e2e/google-auth-signin.cy.ts"`
2. Verify all 11 test cases pass:
   - Google button renders on /auth (sign-up and sign-in tabs)
   - Google button renders on /signin and /signup standalone pages
   - Full landing → auth navigation flow works
   - Tab switching preserves Google button visibility
   - Root redirect to /auth includes Google sign-in
3. Manual testing: Verify Google sign-in popup opens and completes successfully
4. Test in privacy-focused browsers (Safari, Brave) to confirm popup fallback works

## Checklist

- [ ] `pnpm verify` passes
- [ ] No console.logs or debug code
- [ ] Types are complete (no new `any`)
- [ ] Docs updated if needed

author: miclaldogan
body:
## Summary
Prevent IDLE_SLEEP transition when there is recent user activity.

## Problem
`tick()` transitioned from WAKE_ONLY→IDLE_SLEEP based solely on time since entering WAKE_ONLY state. It didn't check if there was recent audio activity, so the system could go to sleep while the user was speaking (without a wake word match).

## Changes
- Added `since_activity = now - self._last_activity` check
- IDLE_SLEEP transition now requires BOTH `elapsed >= idle_sleep_timeout` AND `since_activity >= idle_sleep_timeout`

Closes #741

author: jordigilh
body:
## Summary

Fixes MinIO S3 integration so developers can use MinIO instead of ODF on resource-constrained OpenShift clusters.

**JIRA:** [FLPATH-3220](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/FLPATH-3220)

### Changes

- **deploy-minio-test.sh**: Expose MinIO Service on port 80 (targetPort 9000) to align with default HTTP/S3 client behavior
- **install-helm-chart.sh**: Set `odf.endpoint`, `odf.port=80`, `odf.useSSL=false` instead of the unused `costManagement.s3Endpoint`; fix credential lookup to parse namespace from FQDN; switch bucket-setup image from `alpine:latest` to `ubi9/ubi-minimal` (avoids Docker Hub rate limits)
- **test_storage.py**: Prioritize MASU pod's `S3_ENDPOINT` env var over ODF route for endpoint discovery (fixes false failures on clusters with both ODF and MinIO)
- **New**: `docs/development/ocp-dev-setup-minio.md` — developer guide for OCP setup with MinIO
- **Updated**: installation docs, README, and doc indexes with MinIO references

### Root Cause

Three compounding issues:
1. `deploy-minio-test.sh` created MinIO Service on port 9000
2. Helm template `cost-onprem.storage.endpoint` returns hostname only (no port)
3. Ingress Go app (minio-go SDK) defaults to port 80 when no port is specified

Additionally, `install-helm-chart.sh` was setting the unused `costManagement.s3Endpoint` value instead of the `odf.*` values that templates actually consume.

## Test Plan

- [x] Full E2E suite (149 tests) passes with MinIO on stress.parodos.dev cluster
- [x] Previously failing storage tests (3 failures) now pass after endpoint discovery fix
- [x] Clean deploy verified: delete namespace → deploy MinIO → install chart → all pods healthy
- [x] No regressions in auth, helm, infrastructure, cost_management, ros, or e2e suites

body:
## Summary
This PR fixes an issue where Celery tasks defined in modules with non-standard names (e.g., `tg_auth_tasks.py`) were not being discovered and registered by the worker. The fix explicitly configures the `include` parameter in the Celery app initialization to ensure all task modules are imported at startup.

## Key Changes
- **Updated `backend/app/workers/__init__.py`**:
  - Added explicit `include` list to `Celery()` initialization with all task modules: `app.workers.tasks` and `app.workers.tg_auth_tasks`
  - Removed the generic `celery_app.autodiscover_tasks(["app.workers"])` call which only discovers modules named `tasks.py` by default
  - Removed redundant `broker_connection_retry_on_startup` configuration (already set in `conf.update()`)

- **Added comprehensive tests in `backend/tests/test_celery_config.py`**:
  - Test to verify all expected task modules are in the `include` list
  - Parametrized tests to verify individual tasks from `tg_auth_tasks` are properly registered (`send_code_task`, `confirm_code_task`, `confirm_password_task`)
  - Parametrized tests to verify standard tasks from `tasks.py` remain registered (`campaign_dispatch`, `account_health_check`, `start_warming`)

## Implementation Details
The root cause was that `autodiscover_tasks()` uses a naming convention that only finds modules named `tasks.py`. By explicitly listing modules in the `include` parameter, we ensure all task definitions are discovered regardless of their module name. The tests serve as a guard against future regressions where tasks might be silently skipped due to module discovery issues.

author: copilot
body:
The codegen pipeline was writing files to incorrect paths due to unparsed prefixes in file_map keys, and the deploy agent was generating invalid Kubernetes YAML from LLM responses containing malformed patterns like `type: <PERSON>ports:`.

## Changes

### File Path Cleaning (`server/services/omnicore_service.py`)

Strip `generated/` and `custom_output_dir/` prefixes from file_map keys before materialization to prevent double-nesting:

```python
# Before: generated/hello_generator/generated/app/main.py (double-nested)
# After:  generated/hello_generator/app/main.py (correct)

cleaned_file_map = {}
for original_path, content in result.items():
    cleaned_path = original_path
    if cleaned_path.startswith("generated/"):
        cleaned_path = cleaned_path[len("generated/"):]
    if custom_output_dir and cleaned_path.startswith(f"{custom_output_dir}/"):
        cleaned_path = cleaned_path[len(custom_output_dir) + 1:]
    cleaned_file_map[cleaned_path] = content
```

### YAML Sanitization (`generator/agents/deploy_agent/deploy_response_handler.py`)

Detect and fix malformed YAML patterns in `_sanitize_yaml_response()`:

```python
# Transforms: "  type: <PERSON>ports:"
# Into:       "  type: LoadBalancer\n    ports:"

match = re.match(r'^(\s*)([\w-]+):\s*<[^>]+>(.+)$', line)
if match:
    indent, key, remainder = match.groups()
    if ':' in remainder:
        next_key = remainder.split(':')[0].strip()
        default_value = "LoadBalancer" if key == "type" else "PLACEHOLDER"
        lines.extend([f"{indent}{key}: {default_value}", f"{indent}  {next_key}:"])
```

## Notes

README requirements, Sphinx documentation paths, and critique report locations were already correct in the codebase.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

# Fix Output Directory, YAML Generation, and Missing Artifacts

## Problem Summary
The previous PR (#4) fixed some contract violations but **actual generated output still fails** due to:

1. **Output directory materialization bug** - Files written to wrong paths (e.g., `generated/app/` instead of `generated/hello_generator/app/`)
2. **Kubernetes YAML generation corrupted** - Deploy agent produces invalid YAML with syntax errors
3. **Missing artifacts** - README remains placeholder, docs not generated, reports incomplete

## Root Causes (from code analysis + logs)

### Issue 1: Output Directory Path Construction
**Location**: `server/services/omnicore_service.py:1354-1388`

The code correctly strips `generated/` prefix:
```python
if custom_output_dir.startswith("generated/"):
    custom_output_dir = custom_output_dir[len("generated/"):]
```

BUT the path construction then becomes:
```python
output_path = (base_uploads_dir / job_id / "generated" / custom_output_dir).resolve()
```

**Problem**: If `custom_output_dir = "hello_generator"`, the final path is:
- `uploads/{job_id}/generated/hello_generator/` ✅ CORRECT

But the **materialization** is writing files to paths like:
- `generated/app/main.py` (from file_map keys)

Instead of prepending the correct base directory.

**Log Evidence**:
```
Materialized: app/main.py (150 bytes)
```

The materialization receives a `file_map` with keys like `"app/main.py"` but it's NOT being written relative to the correct `output_dir`.

### Issue 2: Kubernetes YAML Syntax Error
**Location**: `generator/agents/deploy_agent/deploy_response_handler.py:1434` + Kubernetes plugin

**Log Evidence**:
```
ruamel.yaml.scanner.ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here
  in "<unicode string>", line 62, column 22:
    type: <PERSON>ports:
                       ^ (line: 62)
```

The LLM is generating invalid YAML with:
```yaml
type: <PERSON>ports:  # INVALID - missing newline/proper structure
```

**Root Cause**: The Kubernetes template (`deploy_templates/kubernetes_default.jinja`) instructs the LLM to generate "pure YAML" but doesn't have strict enough validation/cleanup in `YAMLHandler._sanitize_yaml_response()`.

### Issue 3: Missing Artifacts

#### a) README is Placeholder
**Location**: README generation in codegen agent

The generated README only contains section headers, no actual content. The template likely needs enhancement.

#### b) Missing Docs
**Location**: `generator/agents/docgen_agent/docgen_agent.py:998-1034`

The Sphinx build IS attempted (fixed in PR #4), but the docs are **not being copied** to the final output directory.

**Code shows**:
```python
self.docs_dir = repo_path_obj / "docs"
self.build_dir = repo_path_obj / "docs" / "_build"
```

But the final output directory (`generated/hello_generator/`) doesn't receive the `docs/` folder.

#### c) Missing critique_report.json
**Location**: `server/services/omnicore_service.py:3151-3207`

The critique report IS generated with required fields (fixed in PR #4), but it's saved to:
```python
report_path = output_dir / "critique_report.json"  # Wrong location
```

Should be:
```python
report_path = output_dir / "reports" / "critique_report.json"
```

---

## Required Fixes

### Fix 1: Correct Output Directory Materialization
**File**: `generator/runner/runner_file_utils.py:1319-1340`

Ensure `materialize_file_map()` writes files with the `output_dir` as the BASE path, not mixed with file_map keys.

**Current code** (lines 1322-1328):
```python
# Compute full path (already validated to be within output_dir)
file_path = (output_dir / relative_path).resolve()
```

This is CORRECT. The bug is earlier - the **file_map keys** likely contain prefixes like `"generated/app/main.py"` when they should just be `"app/main.py"`.

**Real fix location**: `server/services/omnicore_service.py:1390-1450` in `_run_codegen` where the file_map is constructed.

**Fix**:
```python
# Strip "generated/" prefix from ALL file map keys
cleaned_file_map = {}
for file_path, content in result_files.items():
    # Remove "generated/" prefix if present
    if file_path.startswith("generated/"):
        file_path = file_path[len("generated/"):]
    # Remove custom_output_dir prefix if present (avoid double-nesting)
    if custom_output_dir and file_path.startswith(f"{custom_output_dir}/"):
        file_path = file_path[len(custom_output_dir) + 1:]
    cleaned_file_map[file_path] = content

# Pass cleaned map to materialization
mat_result = await materialize_file_map(cleaned_file_map, output_path)
```

### Fix 2: Kubernetes YAML Validation & Cleanup
**File**: `generator/agents/deploy_agent/deploy_response_handler.py:1276-1335`

Enhance `YAMLHandler._sanitize_yaml_response()` to detect and fix common LLM errors:

```python
def _sanitize_yaml_response(self, raw: str) -> str:
    """Enhanced YAML sanitization with strict validation."""
    # Existing markdown stripping...
    
    # NEW: Fix common LLM YAML syntax errors
    lines = content.split('\n')
  ...

body:
# `@ongov/ontario-design-system-component-html-generator`

Introduces **`@ongov/ontario-design-system-component-html-generator`**, a new internal package that renders Ontario Design System Stencil components to static HTML samples.

## What it does

- Hydrates each registered ODS component using Stencil’s server‑side renderer and extracts clean, flattened markup with shadow DOM inlined
- Scopes and transforms component styles so output is self‑contained and portable
- Writes one `.html` file per component to a configurable output directory

## API surface

### Library
`generateSamples(config)` returns a typed `SampleGeneratorResult` for programmatic use

### CLI
- `generate` command with flags for:
  - Output directory
  - Style inclusion
  - `--full-document`
- `init` subcommand to scaffold a config file

## `--full-document` mode

When passed, output is wrapped in a complete document with:
- charset + viewport meta
- inline `<style>`
- `<html>`, `<head>`, and `<body>` tags

This makes any generated sample immediately previewable in a browser without additional setup.

## Docs & testing

- Jest unit-test suite covering all core HTML/CSS processing utilities
- Package README is automatically copied to the Docusaurus internal docs site as part of the build via the shared `documentation-helper` script

author: raindrift
body:
# Create Separate Read-Only Elasticsearch API Key for API Services

## Summary
Implements a dual API key system for Elasticsearch access, separating read/write permissions (ingest services) from read-only permissions (API services).

## Changes
- **New Script**: Rename `k8s_recreate_api_key.sh` → `k8s_recreate_api_keys.sh` (plural)
- **Dual Key Creation**: Script now creates both ingest (read/write) and readonly (read-only) API keys
- **Secret Management**: Creates separate secrets:
  - `elasticsearch-api-key[-prod]` - for ingest services (full permissions)
  - `elasticsearch-api-key-readonly[-prod]` - for API services (read-only)
- **Documentation**: Update index README with detailed explanation of the two-key system and permissions
- **Deployment**: Improve `deploy.sh` with kubectl config and Elasticsearch URL handling

## Security Benefits
- **Principle of Least Privilege**: API services get only the permissions they need
- **Separation of Concerns**: Write operations confined to ingest services
- **Reduced Attack Surface**: Compromised API key can't modify data

### Motivation
- Provide a selectable AI data source so the backend can return deterministic mock AI responses during development or proxy to a live AI agent when available.
- Keep AI provider selection centralized and discoverable via configuration and the run entrypoint to make local development and CI testing simpler.

### Description
- Implemented `AIPipelineService` in `app/services/ai_pipeline_service.py` that supports `mock_json` (local JSON file) and `live_agent` (HTTP pass-through) providers with provider-specific error handling.

- Added CLI flags to the run entrypoint `manage.py` (`--ai-provider`, `--ai-endpoint`, `--config`) and updated tests and README to reflect the new behavior and startup selection flow.

body:
## Problem

The magic side navigation component does not account for safe area insets on devices with notches or other screen cutouts (e.g., iPhone with notch, devices with status bars). This causes the navigation to overlap with system UI elements on mobile devices.

## Solution: What PR does

Updated the magic side nav component to respect safe area insets:

1. **Fixed top positioning**: Changed the toggle button's `top` position from a fixed `8px` to `calc(8px + var(--safe-area-top))` to account for the safe area inset at the top of the screen
2. **Fixed mobile padding**: Changed the mobile view's `padding-top` from `0` to `var(--safe-area-top)` to ensure proper spacing below notches or status bars on small screens

These changes ensure the side navigation component properly adapts to devices with notches, status bars, or other screen cutouts by utilizing CSS safe area inset variables.

## Summary

Consolidates the 3-table data model (`analyzer_type` → `analyzer` → `analyzer_configuration`) into a simpler **2-table model** (`analyzer_type` → `analyzer`) by merging all `analyzer_configuration` fields directly into the `analyzer` entity.

### Key changes

- **Liquibase migration** (`027-merge-analyzer-configuration-into-analyzer.xml`): Widens `analyzer.name`, adds config columns (`ip_address`, `port`, `protocol_version`, `test_unit_ids`, `status`, `identifier_pattern`, `last_activated_date`) to `analyzer`, migrates data, drops `analyzer_configuration` table
- **Entity layer**: `AnalyzerConfiguration` entity deleted; all config fields moved to `Analyzer.java` with `AnalyzerStatus` enum
- **DAO/Service layer**: `AnalyzerConfigurationDAO` and `AnalyzerConfigurationService` deleted; methods migrated to `AnalyzerService`/`AnalyzerServiceImpl`
- **REST controllers**: `AnalyzerRestController` adapted to read/write config fields directly on `Analyzer`; preserves all ibacher PR #2767 review improvements (LinkedHashMap, Path API, AnalyzerControllerHelper, batch validation, Javadoc, SLF4J parameterized logging)
- **Plugin integration**: `pluginTypeId` links `Analyzer` → `AnalyzerType`; `isPluginLoaded()` check via `PluginAnalyzerService`; orphan deactivation + legacy linking at startup (`PluginRegistryService`)
- **Frontend**: `AnalyzerForm` updated for `pluginTypeId` field; `AnalyzersList` shows plugin health status
- **Analyzer readers**: `ASTMAnalyzerReader`, `HL7AnalyzerReader`, `SerialAnalyzerReader` adapted to read config from `Analyzer` directly
- **Copilot review fixes**: Dead code removal, narrowed DAO exception handling, precomputed plugin class name Set for O(1) lookups, structured 500 error bodies, edit-mode plugin type filter fix

### Architecture (before → after)

```
BEFORE: analyzer_type → analyzer → analyzer_configuration (3 tables, 1:1 bolt-on)
AFTER:  analyzer_type → analyzer (2 tables, config columns inlined)
```

author: dcramer
body:
Findings were invisible in PR reviews in two scenarios:

1. **Locationless findings** (no `location` field) were filtered out of inline comments. If they triggered `failOn`, the review body just said "Findings exceed the configured threshold" with no details about what was actually blocking.

2. **Out-of-diff locations** where a finding's line wasn't in the PR diff caused GitHub to reject the entire `createReview` call with 422. The catch block swallowed the error, making all findings completely invisible on the PR.

In both cases the action still failed (the `shouldFail` check is independent), but the developer saw no useful information about what was blocking.

**Renderer changes** (`src/output/renderer.ts`):
- Added `renderFindingsBody()` helper that formats findings as markdown for review bodies
- Locationless findings now render in the review body instead of being dropped
- Mixed findings (inline + locationless) include locationless ones in the body alongside inline comments

**Poster changes** (`src/action/review/poster.ts`):
- On 422 line resolution errors, retries with inline comments moved to the review body via `moveCommentsToBody()`
- Non-line-resolution errors still propagate to the outer catch as before

body:
## Summary

This PR implements a new security policy: **ALL surveys are now encrypted by default before publishing**, regardless of subscription tier or whether they collect patient data.

Previously, only surveys collecting patient data required encryption. Now encryption is universal and mandatory, providing consistent security across the entire platform.

## Key Changes

### 🔐 Core Implementation (e44288d)
- **Publish Workflows**: Updated both web UI and API publish endpoints to require encryption for ALL surveys before first publish
- **Auto-encryption**: Organization SSO users now get automatic encryption for all surveys (not just patient data)
- **Tier Distinction**: Clarified that `can_collect_patient_data=False` for FREE tier means no access to `patient_details_encrypted` templates, NOT no encryption
- **Test Fixtures**: Updated all survey fixtures to include proper encryption setup using `set_dual_encryption()`

### 📚 Documentation Updates (fbda888)
- **pricing-summary.md**: Clarified Free tier includes encrypted surveys
- **encryption-for-users.md**: Updated Quick Overview table and Free tier section
- **encryption-technical-reference.md**: Distinguished universal encryption policy from patient data templates
- **business-continuity.md**: Updated Free tier disaster recovery scenarios

### 🎨 User-Facing Templates (8f2ae5f)
- **home.html**: Changed messaging to "Every survey encrypted by default with AES-256-GCM"
- **pricing.html**: Updated Free tier, Pro tier, comparison table, and FAQs to reflect universal encryption

### 🔧 Additional Improvements
- Organisation model refactoring (063b6f5)
- Test fixes (64a5d50)
- Linting improvements (f0394f7)

## Policy Distinction

The implementation maintains a clear distinction:

- 🔒 **Encryption**: ALL surveys, ALL tiers (including FREE)
- 🏥 **Patient Data Templates**: Paid tiers only (Pro and above)

FREE tier users get:
- Up to 3 encrypted surveys
- Password + recovery phrase protection
- Platform-assisted recovery
- ❌ No access to `patient_details_encrypted` templates

Pro+ tier users get:
- Unlimited encrypted surveys  
- ✅ Access to patient data templates (NHS numbers, clinical data, etc.)

## Testing

✅ All 1473 tests passing
- Updated test fixtures with proper encryption
- Fixed publish workflow tests
- Maintained patient data restriction tests

## Breaking Changes

None. Existing published surveys remain unchanged. Only affects new survey publishing flow.

---

**Closes**: N/A (security enhancement)
**Related**: Security review and encryption policy standardization

body:
The @ mention extraction regex only allowed alphanumerics and hyphens `[A-Za-z0-9-]`, excluding underscores. GitHub usernames support underscores.

## Changes

**Updated regex pattern in 3 files:**
- `resolve_mentions.cjs` - mention extraction
- `sanitize_content_core.cjs` - neutralization of all mentions  
- `sanitize_content.cjs` - selective mention filtering

**Pattern change:**
```diff
- /(^|[^\w`])@([A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,37}[A-Za-z0-9])?(?:\/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?)/g
+ /(^|[^\w`])@([A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,37}[A-Za-z0-9])?(?:\/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?)/g
```

Usernames still must start and end with alphanumeric characters per GitHub's constraints.

**Examples now handled:**
- `@user_name` → extracted as `user_name`
- `@github_copilot` → extracted as `github_copilot`
- `@my_org/my_team` → extracted as `my_org/my_team`
- `@user_` → extracted as `user` (trailing underscore excluded)

author: anilcancakir
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `openai-compatible` provider that enables Laravel AI SDK to work with **any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint** — including services that enforce strict JSON Schema validation on tool/function calling parameters (e.g., Google Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Together AI, Perplexity).

## Problem

The current `openai` provider uses Prism's OpenAI handler which targets the **Responses API** (`/responses`). Many AI services expose an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (`/chat/completions`) but are not fully tolerant of non-standard fields in the JSON Schema.

Specifically, Laravel AI SDK's `Schema::toSchema()` injects a `name` field into the schema output:

```php
return ['name' => $this->name, ...$this->schema->toArray()];
```

This `name` field propagates into tool parameter definitions. Standard OpenAI silently ignores it, but strict services reject it:

```
OpenAI Error [400]: Invalid JSON payload received.
Unknown name "name" at 'request.tools[0].function_declarations[0].parameters.properties[0].value'
```

## Solution

### Schema Sanitization Layer
- **`SanitizedObjectSchema`** — Extends `ObjectSchema` and recursively strips `name` and `additionalProperties` fields from the JSON Schema output (following the same pattern as Prism's internal `Gemini\Maps\SchemaMap`)
- **`OpenAiCompatiblePrismGateway`** — Extends `PrismGateway` and overrides `createPrismTool()` to use `SanitizedObjectSchema` instead of `ObjectSchema`

### Provider Architecture
- **`OpenAiCompatibleProvider`** — Implements `TextProvider` + `EmbeddingProvider` with config-driven model names
- **`OpenAiCompatibleEmbeddingGateway`** — Standalone HTTP gateway for embeddings (Prism's Groq handler lacks embedding support, so we bypass Prism for this)
- Maps to `PrismProvider::Groq` internally (Chat Completions format)

## Usage

```php
// config/ai.php — add to providers array
'gemini-openai' => [
    'driver' => 'openai-compatible',
    'key' => env('GEMINI_API_KEY'),
    'url' => 'https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai',
    'models' => [
        'default' => 'gemini-2.0-flash',
        'cheapest' => 'gemini-2.0-flash-lite',
        'smartest' => 'gemini-2.5-pro',
        'embeddings' => 'text-embedding-004',
        'embedding_dimensions' => 768,
    ],
],

// Multiple instances supported — just add more entries with driver: openai-compatible
'together' => [
    'driver' => 'openai-compatible',
    'key' => env('TOGETHER_API_KEY'),
    'url' => 'https://api.together.xyz/v1',
    'models' => [
        'default' => 'meta-llama/Llama-3-70b-chat-hf',
    ],
],
```

```php
use Laravel\Ai\Facades\Ai;

$response = Ai::provider('gemini-openai')->generateText(
    new TextRequest(prompt: 'Hello from Gemini via OpenAI-compatible endpoint!')
);
```

## Files Changed

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `src/Gateway/Prism/SanitizedObjectSchema.php` | Recursive JSON Schema sanitizer (strips `name`, `additionalProperties`) |
| `src/Gateway/Prism/OpenAiCompatiblePrismGateway.php` | Gateway subclass using sanitized schemas for tool params |
| `src/Gateway/OpenAiCompatibleEmbeddingGateway.php` | Standalone HTTP embedding gateway |
| `src/Providers/OpenAiCompatibleProvider.php` | Provider class (TextProvider + EmbeddingProvider) |
| `src/Gateway/Prism/PrismGateway.php` | Added `openai-compatible` → `Groq` driver mapping |
| `src/AiManager.php` | Registered `createOpenaiCompatibleDriver` factory method |
| `tests/Unit/Gateway/OpenAiCompatiblePrismGatewayTest.php` | Schema sanitization unit tests |
| `tests/Unit/Providers/OpenAiCompatibleProviderTest.php` | Provider resolution + config unit tests |

## Design Decisions

1. **Why not modify `Schema::toSchema()`?** — The `name` field is intentional for OpenAI's Responses API. Removing it globally would break the standard `openai` provider.

2. **Why `SanitizedObjectSchema` instead of a ToolMap?** — Prism's tool serialization happens inside vendor code. Intercepting at the Schema level (before Prism processes it) is the cleanest extension point without modifying vendor.

3. **Why standalone embedding gateway?** — Prism's Groq provider throws `unsupportedProviderAction` for embeddings. A standalone HTTP gateway (following `VoyageAiGateway` pattern) is the established pattern for this case.

4. **Why map to `PrismProvider::Groq`?** — Groq's Prism handler uses the Chat Completions format (`/chat/completions`), which is exactly what OpenAI-compatible services expect. The `Provider` enum has no `OpenAICompatible` case, and adding one would require modifying `prism-php/prism`.

5. **No default config entry** — `openai-compatible` is a protocol, not a specific service. Users add their own named entries with `'driver' => 'openai-compatible'`.

## Tests

- 17 unit tests, 61 assertions — all passing
- Pint: zero violations
- Pre-existing integration test failures (invalid API keys) unrelated to this change

author: jasonyemsft
body:
Let the CI run for azure-deploy tests emit the following output data:
1. Artifacts in the `reports/` folder, including agentMetadata.md of each test run, Copilot CLI logs, the consolidated report markdown for each test and the aggregated report markdown for all tests.
2. Content of the aggregated report markdown, or the consolidated report markdown when there is only 1 test, will be written to the CI job summary.

The AI generated report may show conflicting results compared to the programmatic evaluation conditions. This is because AI cannot reliably tell if a specific skill has been invoked. However, it can tell most of the time if the application has been deployed successfully or not. AI is also not able to differentiate tools vs. skills. It may treat tool calls as skill invocations in the report.

body:
### Motivation
- Fix incorrect Practice Status values (Quota, Collected, Service Level, CDB) that were caused by hardcoded column indices when the table layout changed. 
- Reduce noisy false-error logging from the offscreen scraper and make the panel robust to offscreen timeouts by using a tab-based fallback and stored cache.
- Ensure the panel waits for or rebuilds the practice cache so autocomplete, CDB search, and status display remain consistent.

### Description
- Replaced hardcoded `td:nth-child(...)` extraction with header-based mapping in `MailroomNavigator/offscreen.js` and `MailroomNavigator/background.js` so fields (`ods`, `cdb`, `ehrType`, `collectionQuota`, `collectedToday`, `serviceLevel`) are derived by matching table header text. 
- Added `scrapePracticeListViaTab()` and `loadCacheFromStorage()` in `MailroomNavigator/background.js` and updated `fetchAndCachePracticeList()` to try offscreen scraping first, fall back to a tab scrape, and reuse stored cache on errors. 
- Introduced `syncPracticeCache()` in `MailroomNavigator/panel.js` to deduplicate cache loads, support forced refreshes, and wired input/focus/click handlers to await cache readiness; the manual refresh and periodic scan now use this function. 
- Improved navigator behavior in `MailroomNavigator/navigator.js` by making `normalizePracticeSelection()` more tolerant (trim/case-insensitive name matching) and by using case-insensitive matching for CDB filtering while selecting practices directly from CDB picks. 
- Lowered offscreen timeout noise by changing the offscreen timeout log from `console.error` to `console.warn` so fallbacks are less alarming. 
- Addressed inline review points about misaligned columns and missing fields by mapping via header text and adding compatibility fallbacks for empty caches.

### Testing
- Ran `node --check MailroomNavigator/background.js` which completed successfully. 
- Ran `node --check MailroomNavigator/offscreen.js` which completed successfully. 
- Attempted an automated UI smoke test via Playwright to capture `panel.html`, but the headless browser crashed in this environment (SIGSEGV) so no screenshot artifact was produced; the crash is environmental and not due to the code changes.

body:
## Summary
The branch `feat/implement-providers` implements a significant expansion of the RulePort ecosystem, adding support for multiple new rule sources and targets. The changes are architecturally sound, following the established Source -> IR -> Target pattern.

## Key Changes

### 1. New Source Adapters
Added support for importing rules from:
- **Claude Code** (`.claude/rules/*.md`)
- **Copilot** (`.github/instructions/*.md`)
- **Antigravity** (`.agent/rules/*.md`)
- **Kiro** (`.kiro/steering/*.md`)
- **Windsurf** (`.windsurf/rules/*.md`)

Implementation in `src/sources/*.ts` consistently handles:
- Directory traversal
- Frontmatter parsing (mapping provider-specific fields like `paths`, `inclusion`, `trigger` to standard `globs` and `alwaysApply`)
- Body extraction

### 2. New Target Adapters
Added support for exporting rules to:
- **Cursor** (`.cursor/rules/*.md`)
- **Kiro** (`.kiro/steering/*.md`)
- **Windsurf** (`.windsurf/rules/*.md`)
- **Antigravity** (`.agent/rules/*.md` + `GEMINI.md`)
- **Claude** (`.claude/rules/*.md` + `CLAUDE.md`)

Implementation in `src/targets/*.ts` correctly formats frontmatter and handles provider-specific file structures (consolidated files vs individual files).

### 3. Core Architecture
- **RuleIR**: Updated `RuleSource` and `RuleTarget` types in `src/core/ir.ts` to include new providers.
- **Configuration**: Updated `PathConfig` in `src/config/types.ts` to manage paths for all new providers.

### 4. Testing
- **Sources**: `tests/sources.test.ts` provides comprehensive coverage for all new source adapters, verifying loading, parsing, and error handling.
- **Targets**: `tests/targets.test.ts` covers all new target adapters, ensuring correct file generation, frontmatter formatting, and content inclusion.

author: moltboie
body:
## Summary

This PR refactors the postgres library to use a consistent, type-safe model architecture.

## Changes

### New Architecture
```
postgres/
├── client.ts          # (unchanged)
├── index.ts           # Updated exports
├── initialize.ts      # Uses schemas for table creation
├── database.ts        # Generic query helpers
├── models/
│   ├── common.ts      # Column name constants
│   ├── base.ts        # Type checkers, ModelValidationError
│   ├── user.ts
│   ├── session.ts
│   ├── item.ts
│   ├── account.ts     # + holdings, institutions, securities
│   ├── transaction.ts # + investment/split transactions
│   ├── budget.ts      # + sections, categories
│   ├── snapshot.ts
│   ├── chart.ts
│   └── index.ts
└── repositories/
    ├── users.ts
    ├── accounts.ts
    ├── transactions.ts
    ├── budgets.ts
    ├── snapshots.ts
    ├── charts.ts
    ├── items.ts
    ├── session.ts
    └── index.ts
```

### Key Improvements

1. **Model Classes** - Each entity has a class with:
   - Constructor that validates via `assertType`
   - Static schema defining PostgreSQL column types
   - Column name constants for type safety
   - `toJSON()` method for DB→JSON conversion

2. **Generic Query Helpers** (`database.ts`):
   - `prepareQuery` - Dynamic WHERE clause generation
   - `buildInsert` - INSERT query builder
   - `buildUpdate` - UPDATE query builder  
   - `buildUpsert` - UPSERT (ON CONFLICT) query builder
   - `getTableCreationQuery` - Table creation from schema

3. **Type Safety**:
   - No `any` types used
   - Existing `JSON*` types from `common` remain the contract
   - `ModelValidationError` for catchable validation errors

4. **Schema-driven Initialization**:
   - Table creation now uses model schemas
   - Constraints and indexes defined in models

## Stats
- 23 files changed
- ~7,400 lines added
- TypeScript compiles with zero errors

## References
- Pattern inspired by [storage repo sqlite models](https://github.com/hoiekim/storage/blob/main/src/server/lib/sqlite/models/metadata.ts)

author: copilot
body:
Firestore queries were executing without client-side authentication checks, causing `[cloud_firestore/permission-denied]` errors when security rules rejected unauthenticated requests.

## Changes

### Security Rules (`firestore.rules`)
- Replaced wildcard auth check with collection-specific role-based access control
- Added helper functions: `isAuthenticated()`, `isAdmin()`, `isDriver()`, `isOwner()`
- Defined granular permissions for users, drivers, loads, pods, expenses, invoices, statistics

### Service Layer Authentication Guards
Added pre-flight auth validation to 80+ methods across 5 services:
- `FirestoreService` (30+ methods)
- `ExpenseService` (8 methods)
- `InvoiceService` (9 methods)
- `StatisticsService` (4 methods)
- `DriverExtendedService` (29 methods)

**Pattern applied:**
```dart
class FirestoreService {
  final FirebaseAuth _auth = FirebaseAuth.instance;
  
  void _requireAuth() {
    if (_auth.currentUser == null) {
      throw FirebaseAuthException(
        code: 'unauthenticated',
        message: 'User must be signed in to access Firestore data',
      );
    }
  }
  
  Future<void> someMethod() async {
    _requireAuth();  // Fail fast before network call
    await _db.collection('...').get();
  }
}
```

### Documentation
- `FIRESTORE_AUTHENTICATION_GUIDE.md` - Error handling patterns for UI components (StreamBuilder/FutureBuilder)
- `FIRESTORE_PERMISSION_FIX_SUMMARY.md` - Implementation details and security improvements
- `FIRESTORE_AUTH_QUICK_REFERENCE.md` - Developer quick reference

## Impact
- **Security**: Double-layer validation (client + server rules)
- **Performance**: Fail-fast before network requests
- **UX**: Clear error messages with actionable feedback vs cryptic permission-denied
- **DX**: Consistent pattern, type-safe exceptions

Deploy rules with `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules` after merge.

author: clayjohn
body: Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/116146 In 4.6 (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/107902) we switched to using only 7 roughness levels by default so that we could have the same number of roughness levels when using the "update once" mode and the "update always mode". We also found it helped alleviate some artifacts along seams using our old seam blending approach. However, by the time we merged the work, we used a different approach for seam blending that didn't suffer from the same issue. In hindsight, we should have switched back to 8 layers. But in testing we didn't notice any issues. In the MRP from #116146, we have a very poorly formed HDR with 2 pixels that are 100x brighter than the next brightest handful of pixel and 10,000 times brighter than the average pixel. This causes really bad undersampling artifacts. Godot does the best it can to handle such HDRIs, but the results are not good (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/116146#issuecomment-3881106748 for example). In 4.5.1, this specific case looked okay because it uses full roughness and the environment map is downsampled so far (2x2 pixels per face) that the undersampling isn't visible. When using a lower roughness however, the problems are obvious. In 4.6, we see an issue since the lowest mip level is 10x10 (8x8 + 1 pixel padding) and thus is slightly higher frequency and is able to show off the undersampling artifacts more. By increasing the roughness levels by one, we decrease the final mip level to 6x6 (4x4 + 1 pixel padding) which much more closely matches the final frequency in 4.5.1. This gives the appearance of removing the artifacts in 4.6-stable. However, I want to strongly note that the generated environment map is **bad** in both cases. The particular case of a fully rough, non-metallic object looks better, but the actual result is still bad overall. That being said, I think we should go ahead with this for 4.7 and 4.6.2 as matching the behaviour in 4.5.1 is important and worth doing on its own since we don't want to regress. Even though it is only going from bad behaviour to worse behaviour. _This PR_ _4.5.1_ _4.6_ In the future https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/108127 will help tremendously. And should pave the way for further optimizations

body:
## Summary

This PR refactors the Kafka + Vault encryption demo to run locally on a laptop, eliminating the dependency on Confluent Cloud SaaS. All infrastructure now runs via Docker Compose with Vault Enterprise.

## 🎯 What Changed

### Infrastructure
- ✅ **Docker Compose setup**: Kafka, Zookeeper, Vault Enterprise 1.21.3, Kafka UI
- ✅ **One-command setup**: `./setup.sh` initializes everything
- ✅ **Clean teardown**: `./teardown.sh` stops all services
- ✅ **Vault Enterprise**: License valid until 2030-11-22

### Automation Scripts
- `scripts/init-vault.sh` - Configures Transit and Transform secrets engines
- `scripts/create-topics.sh` - Creates Kafka topics automatically
- `setup.sh` - Complete environment initialization
- `teardown.sh` - Clean shutdown with optional volume removal

### Configuration
- `.env.example` - Environment variable template
- `getting_started.local.ini` - Local Kafka configuration (no SASL/SSL)
- `docker-compose.yml` - Complete infrastructure definition

### Documentation
- Comprehensive README updates with local setup section
- VALIDATION_REPORT.md - Complete test results
- VAULT_ENTERPRISE_VALIDATION.md - Enterprise setup verification
- VAULT_VERSION_UPDATE.md - Vault 1.21.3 upgrade notes
- LOCAL_DEMO_QUICKSTART.md - Quick reference guide
- docs/REFACTORING_SUMMARY.md - Detailed refactoring notes
- docs/terraform_backup.md - Original Confluent setup preserved

### Testing
- Complete test suite (tests/ directory)
- Unit tests for all Python scripts
- Integration tests for end-to-end workflows

## ✨ What Works

All three demo cases are fully functional:

### Demo 1: Plaintext Messages
```bash
python3 producer.py
```
✅ Produces messages to `purchases` topic visible in Kafka UI

### Demo 2: Per-Field Encryption
```bash
python3 encryptor.py &           # Consumes, encrypts, produces
python3 consumer_from_encrypted.py &  # Consumes, decrypts, displays
python3 producer.py              # Generates traffic
```
✅ Transit encryption (addresses) + Transform FPE (credit cards)

### Demo 3: Large File Transfer
```bash
cp test_file.txt source/
python3 consumer_file_transfer.py &
python3 producer_file_transfer.py
```
✅ Envelope encryption with per-file DEK

## 🚀 Quick Start

```bash
# Clone and navigate
cd protecting_kafka_data_using_vault

# Install dependencies
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt

# Start everything
./setup.sh

# Access services
# Kafka UI: http://localhost:8080
# Vault UI: http://localhost:8200/ui

# Run demos
python3 producer.py

# Stop when done
./teardown.sh
```

## 📊 Service URLs

- **Kafka**: localhost:9092
- **Vault Enterprise**: http://localhost:8200
- **Kafka UI**: http://localhost:8080

## 🎁 Benefits

- ✅ **No external accounts** - Works offline
- ✅ **Faster iteration** - No network latency
- ✅ **Better privacy** - Data stays local
- ✅ **Easy reset** - One command cleanup
- ✅ **Free** - No Confluent Cloud costs
- ✅ **Educational** - See all components working together

## 🔐 Security

- Vault Enterprise license properly excluded (.gitignore)
- No sensitive credentials committed
- API keys configuration templates only
- Environment-specific configs in .env

## 📝 Migration Notes

Original Confluent Cloud setup preserved in `terraform/confluent_terraform/` for reference.

Users can switch between local and cloud by changing `getting_started.ini`:
- Local: Use `getting_started.local.ini` (localhost:9092)
- Cloud: Use Confluent Cloud configuration with SASL_SSL

- [x] Docker Compose startup

- **Transit**: AES-256-GCM encryption
- **Transform**: Format-preserving encryption (FPE)

All aspects of the refactoring are documented:
- Setup instructions

None for existing users. This is a new local setup option that coexists with the original Confluent Cloud configuration.

body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the divergence between room-level and thread-level unread indicators in the matrix-react-sdk (v3.62.0) notification system. The existing unread detection logic contained multiple defects producing false-positive and false-negative unread states when rooms contain threaded conversations.

## Key Changes

### Core Unread Detection (`src/Unread.ts`)
- **Rewrote `doesRoomHaveUnreadMessages()`** to evaluate both room main timeline AND each thread independently
- **Removed `feature_thread` guard** around self-sent exclusion so the check applies unconditionally
- **Removed thread-receipt short-circuit** (`return false` when receipt points to threaded event) that caused false negatives
- **Added `doesTimelineHaveUnreadMessages()` helper** encapsulating backward timeline walk with proper filtering
- **Added `doesRoomOrThreadHaveUnreadMessages()` export** for thread-specific Bold detection in hooks
- **Added thread enumeration** via `room.getThreads()` with per-thread receipt resolution using `thread.has()`

### Notification Stores
- **`ThreadNotificationState.ts`**: Replaced `room.getReadReceiptForUserId()` (room-level) with `room.getEventReadUpTo()` + thread-scoped position verification
- **`ThreadsRoomNotificationState.ts`**: Added `NotificationColor.Bold` to severity scan (Red > Grey > Bold > None)
- **`RoomNotificationState.ts`**: Fixed listener cleanup symmetry in `destroy()` — `UnreadNotifications` listener now removed unconditionally

### React Hook
- **`useUnreadNotifications.ts`**: Extended Bold detection to thread-scoped context via `doesRoomOrThreadHaveUnreadMessages(room, threadId)` when `threadId` is supplied

### Test Coverage (94 new/extended tests, all passing)
- Extended `test/Unread-test.ts` (28 tests) — thread-aware unread, self-sent, redacted, multi-thread, edge cases
- Created `test/stores/notifications/ThreadNotificationState-test.ts` (28 tests)
- Created `test/stores/notifications/ThreadsRoomNotificationState-test.ts` (6 tests)
- Extended `test/stores/notifications/RoomNotificationState-test.ts` (7 tests)
- Created `test/hooks/useUnreadNotifications-test.ts` (16 tests)
- Extended `test/components/views/rooms/NotificationBadge/UnreadNotificationBadge-test.tsx` (9 tests)
- Updated `RoomTile-test.tsx.snap` to reflect corrected unread behavior

## Validation Results
- **Build**: 1,167 files compiled successfully via Babel (22s)
- **TypeScript**: 0 errors in in-scope files (5 pre-existing errors in out-of-scope files)
- **Tests**: 3,184/3,184 passed, 0 failures (346 suites)
- **In-scope tests**: 94/94 passed across 6 test suites

## Requirements Implemented
All 14 feature rules (R-001 through R-014) verified: composite timeline evaluation, self-sent exclusion, redacted/non-renderable event filtering, thread-scoped receipt honoring, multi-thread independence, receipt edge cases, no new interfaces, feature flag respect, notification priority preservation, backward compatibility, repository conventions, and test coverage.

## Stats
- 12 files changed | +2,236 / -65 lines | 15 commits
- No new dependencies | No interface changes | No UI/CSS changes
